mainTopic: מוסף for an individual, forgetting ראש חודש in the עמידה, the end of the chapter תפלת השחר, and the new משנה about praying with כובד ראש.
overview: The amud opens as שמואל finishes saying that he prayed מוסף alone only once, on a day when no community prayer took place in נהרדעא. That fits רבי יהודה's view, in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, that an individual in a town with a חבר עיר is exempt from מוסף. רבי ינאי sharply rejects that view. רבי יוחנן testifies that he saw רבי ינאי pray twice, and the proof survives a challenge. Another tradition, from רב, says the הלכה does follow רבי יהודה. A story about רבי חייא בר אבא praying twice leads to a rule: an individual who forgets ראש חודש repeats the עמידה, though in ערבית nobody repeats, in any month. After the הדרן, the new chapter's משנה teaches that one may begin to pray only with כובד ראש, and that one does not interrupt the prayer even for a king or a snake. The גמרא tests several פסוקים as the source and settles on 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה'. It then shows through stories that joy must always come with some trembling.

steps.title: שמואל finishes describing the one time he prayed מוסף alone
steps.stepSummary: שמואל ends his report: he prayed מוסף alone only once, on the day the king's army came to נהרדעא and the רבנן could not hold community prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: In נהרדעא, except for that one day when the king's army came to town. The rabbis were thrown into disorder and did not pray together, so I prayed alone. I was an individual not praying with a חבר עיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story שמואל began just before this section: in נהרדעא he never said מוסף alone except on one unusual day. He did it on that day only because there was no community prayer at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's wording suggests he usually avoided saying מוסף alone when a community was praying, which matches רבי יהודה's view in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The one exception happened only because there was no חבר עיר praying that day. This sets up the next steps, where other חכמים argue about whether that view is the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: A major Jewish city in Babylonia where שמואל lived and taught
They were busy or thrown into disorder
An individual praying alone, not with the community
The town's community group; here, communal prayer

steps.confusionAlert: This section starts in the middle of a sentence. The words just before it in the גמרא are שמואל saying that he never prayed מוסף alone. So 'in נהרדעא' is the continuation of that thought.

phrases.english: In Neharde'a, except for that day
when the king's army came to the town,
and the rabbis were preoccupied and did not pray,
and I prayed as an individual,
and I was an individual not in a community group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes שמואל's statement, which began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל said מוסף alone only when no community prayer took place, which fits רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: רבי חנינא קרא rules like רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא קרא, sitting before רבי ינאי, states that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה quoting רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא קרא was sitting before רבי ינאי. He sat and said: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who said it in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: A student rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה: in a town that has a חבר עיר, an individual is exempt from מוסף. This sets up רבי ינאי's sharp reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling matches what שמואל did in step 1. It is stated in front of רבי ינאי, who is about to reject it. So this step is the claim the next step will push back against.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert in reading תנ״ך; part of רבי חנינא's title

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי חֲנִינָא קָרָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina the Bible expert sat before Rabbi Yannai,
phrases.notes: קָרָא here is a title: someone expert in reading the פסוקים, not the word for 'verse.'

phrases.english: and he sat and said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי חֲנִינָא קָרָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts forward as הלכה the view that שמואל followed in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: an individual in a town with a חבר עיר is exempt from מוסף.

steps.title: רבי ינאי sharply rejects that ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי tells רבי חנינא קרא to take his ruling outside, because the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go read your verses outside, because the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה, who said it in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי firmly rejects the ruling from step 2. He says the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Go read your verses outside' is a sharp put-down. It means this ruling does not belong in the בית המדרש, so stick to reading פסוקים. The point is that an individual must say מוסף even in a town that has a חבר עיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבי ינאי's position: an individual is required to pray מוסף. Step 8 brings a tradition from רב that rules the other way.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פּוּק קְרֵא קְרָאָיךְ לְבָרָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go out, read your verses outside,
phrases.notes: A sharp reply that plays on his title קָרָא: go read פסוקים, but don't rule הלכה in here.

phrases.english: for the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the ruling given in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It does not match the accepted הלכה; an individual must say מוסף.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן saw רבי ינאי pray twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן testifies that he saw רבי ינאי pray and then pray again, which suggests he said מוסף even alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: I saw רבי ינאי pray, and then pray again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings evidence from what רבי ינאי actually did. He prayed a second time, which seems to have been מוסף said alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second prayer was מוסף, then רבי ינאי's practice matches his ruling in step 3. It would show that an individual says מוסף even in a town that has a חבר עיר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
I saw Rabbi Yannai
who prayed and then prayed again.
phrases.notes: The assumption is that the first prayer was שחרית and the second was מוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי ינאי's ruling with evidence from his own practice
steps.raayaObject: That an individual says מוסף even in a town that has a חבר עיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן saw רבי ינאי pray a second time

steps.title: Maybe the second prayer was just a repeat
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא: maybe רבי ינאי repeated his first prayer because he lacked כוונה the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: But maybe at first he did not focus his mind, and then he focused his mind the second time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה questions the proof from step 4. Maybe the second prayer was not מוסף at all, just a better-focused redo of the first prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second prayer was a repeat for כוונה, it tells us nothing about מוסף. Then the proof that an individual must say מוסף falls apart.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
But perhaps initially he did not focus his mind
and ultimately he focused his mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from רבי יוחנן's testimony
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי ינאי's second prayer was מוסף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second prayer could have been a repeat of the first one, done with proper כוונה.

steps.title: Look who is testifying
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that a witness as great as רבי יוחנן would have known what kind of prayer it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Look how great the man is who is testifying about him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends the proof. רבי יוחנן was a great authority, so he surely understood correctly that the second prayer was מוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer relies on how reliable the witness is. רבי יוחנן would not report this as meaningful unless he was sure it was מוסף. So the proof from step 4 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ינאי ruled, and acted, as one who says מוסף even alone. In his view the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. Step 8 brings רב's opposing tradition.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזִי מַאן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה
phrases.english: He said to him: See who the great man is
who is testifying about him.
phrases.notes: The great man is רבי יוחנן, who would have known exactly what he saw.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזִי מַאן גַּבְרָא רַבָּה דְּקָמַסְהֵיד עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relies on the witness being reliable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second prayer may have been a repeat for כוונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן would only testify if he was sure the second prayer was מוסף.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי prayed where they learned
steps.stepSummary: טבריא had thirteen synagogues, but רבי אמי and רבי אסי prayed only between the columns where they studied.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי had thirteen synagogues in טבריא. Even so, they prayed only between the columns, where they studied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new report about how חכמים prayed. These two rabbis chose to pray in their study hall rather than in a synagogue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves away from the מוסף question to a related subject: the best place to pray. Their choice shows they valued praying in the place where they learned תורה, even with many synagogues nearby.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi,
even though they had
thirteen synagogues in Tiberias,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲווֹ מְצַלּוּ אֶלָּא בֵּינֵי עַמּוּדֵי,
phrases.english: would pray only between the columns,
where they would study.
phrases.notes: 'Between the columns' is the study hall where they learned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲווֹ לְהוּ תְּלֵיסַר בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא בִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reports about how חכמים prayed, now about where they prayed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי and רבי אסי prayed only in their place of Torah study, not in the synagogues.

steps.title: רב's tradition: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה's version
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי reports in the name of רב that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who quoted רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב יצחק בר אבדימי said in the name of our teacher (רב): the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who said it in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a formal ruling on the question of תפלת המוספין that the earlier steps were discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי ינאי said the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה here. Now a different tradition, from רב, says it does. So the two traditions disagree about the practical ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the ruling on תפלת המוספין was itself debated among the אמוראים, which sets the background for the story that follows.

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ אָמַר:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi said in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" here means רב.

phrases.english: The halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: who said it in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that runs against רבי ינאי's position from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה's report of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view on תפלת המוספין.

steps.title: Why did רבי חייא בר אבא pray twice?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא prayed and then prayed again, and רבי זירא asks him why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא prayed, and then prayed again. רבי זירא said to him: Why did you, my master, do that?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins: a sage prays twice, and his colleague asks for the reason. This sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the עמידה needs a reason, and רבי זירא wants to know what it was. In the next steps he tries out possible reasons on his own.

keyTerms.meaning: "Master": a polite way of saying "you" to a sage

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא צַלִּי וַהֲדַר צַלִּי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba prayed and then prayed again.
Rabbi Zeira said to him:
Why did the master do this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story about repeating a prayer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רבי חייא בר אבא repeated his תפלה

steps.title: It could not have been for lack of concentration
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא rules out a lack of כוונה as the reason, because רבי אליעזר taught that a person who cannot concentrate should not pray at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it was because you did not concentrate, didn't רבי אליעזר say: A person should always check himself. If he can focus his heart, he should pray. If not, he should not pray.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא suggests one possible reason, a lack of כוונה, and knocks it down himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, a person who knows he cannot focus should not start praying in the first place. So a great sage like רבי חייא would not have prayed without focus and then needed to repeat. That reason is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say...": brings up a possible answer, usually to reject it
"A person should measure himself", checking whether he can concentrate
To focus one's heart, having כוונה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 5. There, a lack of כוונה was raised as a possible reason for רבי ינאי's second prayer. Here, רבי זירא himself rejects that reason using רבי אליעזר's teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא כַּוֵּון מָר דַּעְתֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: If you say it is because the master did not focus his mind,
but didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
A person should always measure himself;

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ — יִתְפַּלֵּל,
phrases.english: if he can focus his heart, he should pray,
and if not, he should not pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא כַּוֵּון מָר דַּעְתֵּיהּ, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one possible answer to the question in step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the second prayer was because of missing כוונה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A person without focus should not pray at all, so he would never end up needing to repeat for that reason

steps.title: Maybe he forgot to mention ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests a different reason: רבי חייא forgot to mention ראש חודש in his first תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be that you did not mention ראש חודש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא offers a second possible reason for the repeated prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day was ראש חודש, and on it we add a special mention of the day (יעלה ויבוא) in the תפלה. Forgetting it might seem to require praying again. The next step tests this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: ראש חודש, the start of the month

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּלָא אַדְכַּר מָר דְּרֵישׁ יַרְחָא.
phrases.english: Rather, the master did not mention the New Moon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּלָא אַדְכַּר מָר דְּרֵישׁ יַרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from step 10 with a new one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeat was because he forgot to mention ראש חודש

steps.title: But forgetting ראש חודש does not require repeating
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges his own suggestion with a ברייתא: a person who forgets ראש חודש does not go back, because he can mention it in the next תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: If someone made a mistake and did not mention ראש חודש: in ערבית we do not make him go back, because he can say it in שחרית. In שחרית we do not make him go back, because he can say it in מוסף. In מוסף we do not make him go back, because he can say it in מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ראש חודש explanation from step 11 using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a person who forgot ראש חודש never has to repeat, because the next תפלה of the day will include the mention. If so, forgetting ראש חודש cannot explain why רבי חייא prayed again.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not make him go back and repeat

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: But it was taught: If he erred and did not mention the New Moon,
in the evening prayer, we do not make him go back,
because he can say it in the morning prayer.
In the morning prayer, we do not make him go back,
because he can say it in the additional prayer.
In the additional prayer, we do not make him go back,
because he can say it in the afternoon prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation offered in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that forgetting ראש חודש caused the repeated prayer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says forgetting ראש חודש never requires repeating, since it can be said in the next תפלה

steps.title: That rule applies only when praying with a congregation
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that רבי יוחנן limited the ברייתא to prayer with a ציבור, so a person praying alone who forgets does repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wasn't it stated about that ברייתא that רבי יוחנן said: They taught it about a ציבור?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא defends the ראש חודש explanation by narrowing what the ברייתא covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, the 'no need to go back' rule is about prayer in a communal setting. An individual praying on his own who forgot ראש חודש does have to repeat. That is why רבי חייא prayed again.

keyTerms.meaning: "Wasn't it stated about it?": brings a later teaching that limits a source

steps.whatToRemember: Forgetting ראש חודש: in a ציבור you do not go back, but an individual praying alone does repeat. That is why רבי חייא בר אבא prayed twice.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wasn't it stated about it:
phrases.notes: The one answering is רבי חייא בר אבא, and "it" is the ברייתא from the last step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: They taught this about a congregation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to mean that nobody ever repeats for forgetting ראש חודש
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone praying with a ציבור does not repeat; an individual does repeat

steps.title: How long should one wait between two prayers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much time a person should pause between a first תפלה and a second one.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long should a person wait between one תפלה and the next?
steps.whatsHappening: Following the story of praying twice, the גמרא asks a practical question. This sets up the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who must pray twice in a row, like רבי חייא, should not start the second תפלה right away. The question is how long the gap should be.

phrases.english: How long should one wait between one prayer and the next?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grows out of the story of praying twice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of the pause needed between two consecutive תפלות

steps.title: Wait until the mind is ready to plead again
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא answer: wait long enough that the mind is ready to plead (תתחונן) or to beseech (תתחולל) again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא: One said: long enough that his mind is in a pleading mood. The other said: long enough that his mind is in a beseeching mood.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question, each with his own wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is not a set number of minutes. It is a state of mind: the person should wait until he can truly ask ה׳ again. The two words, תתחונן and תתחולל, express close ideas in different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: "One said... and one said": two opinions without saying which sage said which
That his mind be in a pleading mood (from תחנונים, pleas)
That his mind be in a beseeching mood

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְחוֹנֵן דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: One said: long enough for his mind to be in a pleading mood,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְחוֹלֵל דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: and one said: long enough for his mind to be in a beseeching mood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא. חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wait until the mind is ready to plead or beseech again

steps.title: Both views come from פסוקים about משה's prayers
steps.stepSummary: Each of the two wordings, תתחונן and תתחולל, is tied to a פסוק describing how משה prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said 'so that his mind is ready to plead' learns it from 'And I pleaded to ה׳.' The one who said 'so that his mind is ready to beseech' learns it from 'And משה besought.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where each of the two answers in Step 15 comes from. Each wording matches a word used in the תורה for משה's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא and רב חסדא did not just pick nice words. Each chose a word the תורה uses for משה's prayer: ואתחנן (pleading) and ויחל (beseeching). So both views say the person must reach the frame of mind משה had when he prayed.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who said (refers back to one side of a disagreement)
As it is written (brings a פסוק as a source)
And I pleaded: משה asking ה׳ to let him enter the land
And he besought: משה pleading for the people after the עגל

phrases.english: The one who said: "so that his mind will be ready to plead",
is because it is written: "And I pleaded to ה׳."
phrases.notes: דברים 3:23

phrases.english: And the one who said: "so that his mind will be ready to beseech",
is because it is written: "And משה besought."
phrases.notes: שמות 32:11

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר ״כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּתְחוֹנֵן דַּעְתּוֹ עָלָיו״, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for each of the two wordings in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The two wordings of רב הונא and רב חסדא about the pause between תפלות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ואתחנן אל ה׳ (דברים 3:23) and ויחל משה (שמות 32:11).

steps.title: Forgetting ראש חודש at night: no need to repeat
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if someone forgot to mention ראש חודש in ערבית, he does not go back, because בית דין only sanctifies the month during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said in the name of רב: if someone made a mistake and did not mention ראש חודש in ערבית, we do not make him go back, because בית דין only sanctifies the new month by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of forgetting ראש חודש in the עמידה and brings a new rule from רב about the night prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 13) we learned that a person praying alone who forgets ראש חודש does repeat. רב adds an exception for ערבית. Since the month's holiness is set by בית דין only in the daytime, the night prayer is not tied to it strongly enough to require repeating.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not make him go back and repeat
The court (here, the one that declares the new month)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule: forgetting יעלה ויבוא at night is treated differently from forgetting it by day.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said that Rav said:
If he made a mistake and did not mention
Rosh Chodesh in the evening prayer,
we do not make him go back,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ
phrases.english: because the court does not sanctify the month
except by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ראש חודש topic and adds a rule for the night prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgot ראש חודש in ערבית does not repeat, since the month is sanctified only by day.

steps.title: אמימר limits רב's rule to a full month
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says רב's rule makes sense only in a full month; in a short month, a person who forgets at night must repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: רב's rule makes sense in a full month. But in a short month, we do make him go back.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר narrows רב's rule. He says it applies only in a certain kind of month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a full month (30 days), ראש חודש is two days, so if someone forgets on the first night he still has the second night. After a short month there is only one night of ראש חודש, so there is no second night on which to make it up. For that reason אמימר says he must repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is reasonable
A full month (30 days), followed by two days of ראש חודש
A short month (29 days), followed by one day of ראש חודש

steps.confusionAlert: אמימר is not arguing with רב. He is only limiting when רב's rule applies.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
Rav's statement makes sense in a full month.
phrases.notes: A full month means ראש חודש is two days, so if you forget one night there is still another night.

phrases.english: But in a short month, we make him go back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's rule from Step 17 to a full month.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's rule holds in a full month; in a short month, one who forgot at night repeats.

steps.title: רב אשי: רב's reason applies to every month
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges אמימר: since רב based his rule on a reason, the length of the month should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: רב gave a reason, so what difference does it make to me whether the month is short or full?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks אמימר's limitation. He points back to the reason רב himself gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב did not say 'you get another chance tomorrow night.' He said בית דין only sanctifies the month by day. That reason is true in a short month and in a full month alike, so אמימר's split has no basis in רב's words.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all (opens an argument from something already known)
What difference does it make to me

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
After all, Rav stated a reason,
phrases.notes: The reason is that בית דין only sanctifies the month by day, from Step 17.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי חָסֵר וּמָה לִי מָלֵא?!
phrases.english: so what difference is it to me whether it is short or full?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי רַב טַעְמָא קָאָמַר, מָה לִי חָסֵר וּמָה לִי מָלֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's limitation in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's split between a full month and a short month.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's own reason (sanctifying the month only by day) applies equally to every month, so the month's length cannot change the rule.

steps.title: No difference between short and full months
steps.stepSummary: The conclusion: רב's rule applies to every month, so one who forgets ראש חודש in ערבית never repeats.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי concludes his argument. רב's rule applies to every month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר's limitation is dropped. Whether the month is short or full, someone who forgot ראש חודש in ערבית does not go back.
steps.whatToRemember: If someone forgets ראש חודש in ערבית, he does not repeat, in any month. The reason is that בית דין only sanctifies the month by day.

phrases.english: Rather, there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב אשי's challenge with the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's rule applies in all months: one who forgot ראש חודש in ערבית is not required to repeat.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter תפלת השחר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes the chapter תפלת השחר with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, תפלת השחר!
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter תפלת השחר. It is a closing formula, not a new argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each chapter of the גמרא ends with a הדרן, which expresses the hope to come back and learn this chapter again. Nothing new is ruled here. It simply signals that a new chapter is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the formula said when finishing a chapter
The morning prayer: the name of the chapter just finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, The Morning Prayer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose last discussion (steps 17-20) was about forgetting ראש חודש in ערבית.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter תפלת השחר is complete.

steps.title: The משנה: praying only with a serious, focused mind
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens: one may only begin praying with seriousness. The early חסידים waited an hour first, and once praying, a person does not stop even for a king or a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may only stand up to pray when he is in a serious frame of mind. The early pious people would wait an hour and then pray, so they could focus their hearts on their Father in Heaven. Even if the king greets him, he should not answer. Even if a snake is wrapped around his heel, he should not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The new chapter begins with a משנה about the right state of mind for תפלה. It also teaches that once you are praying, you do not interrupt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has three parts. First, a basic rule: you need כובד ראש before praying. Second, a higher level: the early חסידים spent a whole hour getting ready. Third, the seriousness continues during the prayer itself, so you do not stop for a king's greeting or even a snake on your heel.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: the opening text of the new chapter
Literally 'heaviness of head': a serious, humble, focused mood
The early pious people of earlier generations
They would wait one hour before praying
He should not interrupt or stop his prayer

steps.confusionAlert: The hour of waiting describes what the חסידים did. It is a special level of piety, not the basic minimum. The basic rule is the opening line about כובד ראש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the attitude for all of תפלה, and the rest of the chapter builds on it.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One may not stand to pray
except from a state of seriousness.
phrases.notes: Literally 'heaviness of head.' It means a serious, humble mood, the opposite of light-headedness.

phrases.english: The early pious ones
would wait one hour, and then pray,
so that they would direct their hearts
to their Father in Heaven.
Even if the king greets him,
he should not answer him;
and even if a snake is wrapped around his heel,
he should not stop.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין עוֹמְדִין לְהִתְפַּלֵּל אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ כּוֹבֶד רֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a brand-new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may only begin תפלה with כובד ראש, and once praying one does not interrupt, even for a king's greeting or a snake on one's heel.

steps.title: Asking for the source of praying with seriousness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule about כובד ראש comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the opening rule of the משנה, that one must pray with seriousness. The גמרא wants a פסוק that supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where are these things?': the גמרא asking for a source

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's opening rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that serves as the source for praying only with כובד ראש.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר brings the פסוק about חנה's bitter prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the source is the פסוק about חנה: 'and she was bitter of soul' when she prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The פסוק says, 'And she was bitter of soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question with a פסוק about חנה, who prayed with a heavy, bitter heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה, the mother of שמואל, prayed while feeling deep bitterness. רבי אלעזר learns from her that real תפלה comes from a serious, heavy heart, which is exactly the משנה's כובד ראש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As the פסוק says': introduces a source verse

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
As the verse states: "And she was bitter of soul."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 1:10. 'She' is חנה, praying for a child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is חנה's prayer, described as 'bitter of soul,' showing that תפלה requires a heavy, serious heart.

steps.title: Maybe חנה was a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: חנה may have prayed that way only because she was in deep pain, so her case does not teach a rule for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe חנה is different, since her heart was very bitter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר's proof and argues that חנה's situation was unusual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only tells us how חנה happened to feel, and she was suffering terribly. That describes her personal state. It does not show that every person must pray in such a frame of mind, so the proof falls away and a new source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From what?': how do you know that?

phrases.english: From what do you know this?
Perhaps Hannah is different,
since her heart was very embittered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's source from חנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from חנה. The משנה's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חנה's bitterness came from her personal suffering, so her case cannot serve as a general rule for every person who prays.

steps.title: A new source from דוד entering God's house in awe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא brings a פסוק where דוד says he will bow toward the היכל in awe of God.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: the source is from here: 'And I, through Your great kindness, will come into Your house; I will bow toward Your holy היכל in awe of You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The proof from חנה was just rejected, so the גמרא offers a new source. דוד says he approaches God 'in awe,' which suggests that prayer must start with seriousness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier proof is dropped and a fresh one is coming. The key word is ביראתך, 'in awe of You.' Coming before God in תפלה is like coming into the היכל, so it must be done with awe.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it drops the earlier idea and starts a new one
From here; it introduces the source פסוק
In awe of You; the key word of the proof

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said: it is from here:
"And I, through Your great kindness, will come into Your house;
phrases.notes: תהלים 5:8

phrases.english: I will bow toward Your holy sanctuary in awe of You."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from חנה with a new פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for praying with כובד ראש (from step 23).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד's words 'I will bow toward Your holy היכל in awe of You.'

steps.title: Maybe דוד was a special case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof because דוד may have prayed with extra pain and effort, so he cannot be the model for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Maybe דוד is different, because he would greatly pain himself in his prayers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from דוד. It suggests that דוד's awe was his own special way, not a rule for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of rejection used against חנה in step 25. If a person prays with unusual pain, his example does not prove what an ordinary person must do. So the search for a source goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know? It questions whether the proof really works
Perhaps; it offers another way to see the case

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps David is different,
because he would greatly pain himself in prayers for mercy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source brought in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from דוד is rejected. The rule of כובד ראש itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: דוד's way of praying was unusual, so it may not apply to everyone.

steps.title: A new source: read 'beauty' as 'trembling'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי brings a general פסוק about bowing to God and rereads בהדרת as בחרדת, 'in trembling.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יהושע בן לוי said: the source is from here: 'Bow to God בהדרת קודש.' Do not read בהדרת, 'in beauty'; read instead בחרדת, 'in trembling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source. This פסוק tells everyone how to bow to God, and by rereading one word it teaches that one must come with trembling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes the weakness of the last two proofs. It is not about one special person; it is a command to all. Using the אל תקרי method, הדרת (beauty) is reread as חרדת (trembling), which teaches seriousness.

keyTerms.meaning: Bow down; a command to everyone
Do not read it as; a way of drawing a lesson by rereading a word

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean the פסוק is spelled wrong. The written word stays; the גמרא is reading an extra lesson into it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: it is from here:
"Bow to the Lord in the beauty of holiness."
phrases.notes: תהלים 29:2

phrases.english: Do not read "in the beauty of"
phrases.notes: The two words use almost the same letters, just moved around: הדרת and חרדת.

phrases.english: but rather "in the trembling of."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from דוד with a general command, read through אל תקרי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for praying with כובד ראש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Bow to God בהדרת קודש,' read as בחרדת, 'in trembling.'

steps.title: Maybe it really means beauty, like רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the פסוק may mean 'beauty' as written, teaching that one should dress nicely for תפלה, as רב יהודה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps I can tell you that it really means 'beauty,' as written. This is like רב יהודה, who would dress himself up and then pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reread. It says the plain word, 'beauty,' also makes sense: get ready for prayer by looking nice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the plain meaning works, there is no need to reread הדרת as חרדת. The פסוק could be teaching about dressing well, and רב יהודה's practice shows this reading is real. So it no longer proves anything about seriousness.

keyTerms.meaning: I can really tell you; it keeps the plain meaning

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not rejecting רב יהודה's practice. It uses his practice to show that the plain reading 'beauty' makes sense.

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps I can really tell you
that it means "beauty," literally.
Like this case of Rav Yehuda,
who would adorn himself, and then he would pray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the אל תקרי reading of step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from 'בהדרת קודש' is rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plain meaning, 'beauty,' works fine, as shown by רב יהודה, so the reread is not forced.

steps.title: The source that stands: serve God in awe
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה,' a plain command to all to serve God with awe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the source is from here: 'Serve God in awe, and rejoice with trembling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth source, and this time it is not rejected. The פסוק plainly tells everyone to serve God with awe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proof avoids both earlier problems. It is a general command, not one person's special way, and it says 'awe' outright with no rereading. Prayer is a kind of serving God, so it must be done with seriousness.

keyTerms.meaning: In awe, with fear of Heaven

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule that one must start תפלה with כובד ראש.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: it is from here:
"Serve the Lord in awe,
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:11

phrases.english: and rejoice with trembling."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of step 28 with a plain, general פסוק that is not challenged.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for praying with כובד ראש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה': serve God in awe.

steps.title: What does 'rejoice with trembling' mean?
steps.stepSummary: Now that it quoted the פסוק, the גמרא asks what its second half means, since joy and trembling seem like opposites.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and rejoice with trembling' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain the end of the פסוק it just quoted. It is setting up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joy and trembling sound like they cannot go together. The question asks how a person can do both at once. This is a side point about the פסוק, not a new challenge to the proof.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "and rejoice with trembling"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How joy and trembling can go together in the פסוק.

steps.title: Where there is joy, there should be trembling
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנא, quoting רבה, explains that even in a place of joy a person should keep some trembling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנא said in the name of רבה: in a place of joy, there should be trembling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the פסוק. Joy is allowed, but it should never be wild; some awe must stay with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words do not cancel each other. A person may be happy, but the happiness should come with seriousness. This fits the whole topic of coming to תפלה with awe.
steps.whatToRemember: The source for praying with כובד ראש is 'עבדו את ה׳ ביראה.' The proofs from חנה and דוד were rejected because each was a special case, and 'בהדרת קודש' was rejected because it can mean 'beauty,' as written. The end of the פסוק teaches that even joy should come with trembling.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא אָמַר רַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said that Rabba said:
In a place of rejoicing, there should be trembling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even where there is joy, there should also be trembling.

steps.title: רבה warns אביי about too much joy
steps.stepSummary: רבה sees אביי being very joyful and challenges him with the פסוק 'וגילו ברעדה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was sitting before רבה. רבה saw that he was very joyful, and said: 'It is written, Rejoice with trembling!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that puts רבה's teaching into action. רבה sees his student אביי being very happy and challenges him with the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה had just taught that joy must come with some trembling. Now he applies it: אביי's great joy seems to have no trembling in it. The question is how אביי can act this way when the פסוק says otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting before him, learning in front of his teacher
It is written, used to quote a פסוק

phrases.english: Abaye was sitting before Rabba.
He saw that he was rejoicing very much.
phrases.notes: רבה is the one who saw, and אביי is the one rejoicing.

phrases.english: He said: "Rejoice with trembling" is written!
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:11. This is the same פסוק the גמרא just explained.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבה's teaching from Step 32 in a real story
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק demands trembling together with joy, and אביי seems to show only joy.

steps.title: אביי answers that he is wearing תפילין
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that he is wearing תפילין, so the trembling is already there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I am wearing תפילין.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself in just a few words: he is wearing תפילין right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not deny that joy needs trembling. His point is that wearing תפילין itself keeps a person aware of God, so the 'trembling' part of the פסוק is already being kept. That is why his joy is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Phylacteries, the boxes worn on the head and arm
I am putting on, I am wearing

phrases.english: He said to him: I am wearing tefillin.
phrases.notes: He means the תפילין already give him the awe the פסוק asks for, so he may rejoice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the requirement is already met in this situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's great joy has no trembling and breaks the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wearing תפילין provides the trembling, so his joy is proper.

steps.title: רבי זירא warns רבי ירמיה about too much joy
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא sees רבי ירמיה very joyful and challenges him with the פסוק 'בכל עצב יהיה מותר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה was sitting before רבי זירא. רבי זירא saw that he was very joyful and said to him: 'It is written, In all sorrow there is profit!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story just like the first. This time רבי זירא challenges his student רבי ירמיה, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק from משלי says sorrow brings benefit, which suggests a person should not be overly joyful. It adds a second source to the idea that joy should be held back.

keyTerms.meaning: In all sorrow there is profit (משלי 14:23)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הֲוָה יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting before Rabbi Zeira.
He saw that he was rejoicing very much.
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is the one who saw, and רבי ירמיה is the one rejoicing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״בְּכׇל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר״ כְּתִיב?
phrases.english: He said to him: "In all sorrow there is profit" is written?
phrases.notes: משלי 14:23

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״בְּכׇל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story with the same pattern as Step 33, using a different פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק praises sorrow, so too much joy seems improper.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה gives the same answer about תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers just as אביי did: he is wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'I am wearing תפילין.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers his teacher with exactly the same words אביי used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different students, challenged with two different פסוקים, give the same answer. This shows the idea is solid: wearing תפילין brings enough awe that joy can be expressed freely.
steps.whatToRemember: Joy should always come with some awe of God. When a person is wearing תפילין, that awe is already there, so his joy is fine.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am wearing tefillin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in the same way as Step 34
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the requirement is already met in this situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ירמיה's great joy goes against the פסוק praising sorrow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wearing תפילין supplies the needed awe, so the joy is allowed.

steps.title: Setting the scene: the רבנן are overly joyful at a wedding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new story: at his son's wedding feast, מר בריה דרבינא notices the רבנן becoming excessively joyful.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, the son of רבינא, made a wedding feast for his son. He saw that the רבנן were becoming very, very joyful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story that fits the theme of 'rejoice with trembling.' This line only sets the scene and is preparing for what מר בריה דרבינא will do next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps taught that joy should be mixed with some seriousness. Here we see a real situation where the רבנן went too far in their joy. The problem is set up now so the גמרא can show how a great person reacted to it.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina,
made a wedding feast for his son.
He saw the Sages
who were being very joyful.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא עֲבַד הִילּוּלָא לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the exchanges about רבי ירמיה, אביי, and their תפילין, the גמרא brings another story showing the same idea: joy needs some trembling mixed in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: at a wedding feast the רבנן became overly joyful, creating the need for a reminder to stay serious.
